summary: Halyard mutual NDA with counterparty edits that fill in Kestrel Pay's details, add contractors, restate clause 2.1 in one-way form but restore mutuality in 2.2, extend the return period to 14 Business Days, and ask about backups and a shorter survival period.

findings.quote: [[INS: KESTREL PAY LTD]], a company incorporated and registered in [[INS: England and Wales]] with company number [[INS: 14509218]]
findings.why: The counterparty has completed its entity details, which the lawyer must confirm against the company register.

findings.quote: The obligations and restrictions set out in Clause 2.1 shall apply equally and mutatis mutandis to Halyard in respect of any Confidential Information disclosed to it by or on behalf of the Counterparty
findings.why: Clause 2.1 as edited names only Halyard as discloser, but the inserted 2.2 applies the obligations to both Parties by cross-reference, so the NDA stays mutual.
findings.fallback_cited: Obligations stated once and applied to both parties by cross-reference.

findings.quote: a potential commercial relationship [[INS: concerning API payment processing integration]] between them (the Purpose)
findings.why: The Purpose is still limited to discussions about a commercial relationship, now tied to a named project (API payment processing integration), and use is limited to the Purpose in 2.1.2.
findings.fallback_cited: Purpose limited to a named project, product evaluation or pilot.

findings.quote: which is either marked or identified as confidential at the time of disclosure or would reasonably be considered confidential given the nature of the information and the circumstances of its disclosure
findings.why: The definition covers information disclosed for the Purpose that is marked or reasonably confidential and includes derived notes and analyses.

findings.quote: can demonstrate by written records or other reasonable evidence
findings.why: All four carve-outs (public domain, already held, third-party receipt, independent development) are present and unnarrowed.

findings.quote: the employees, officers, directors, [[INS: contractors,]] professional advisers, auditors and insurers of that Party and of any member of its Group
findings.why: Disclosure to employees, advisers, auditors, insurers and Group members on a need-to-know basis with recipient liability is preserved; adding contractors only widens the Representatives, who stay bound under 4.1.2 and 4.1.3.

findings.quote: to the extent that it is legally permitted to do so
findings.why: Compelled disclosure is permitted, notice and cooperation apply only where legally permitted, and resisting disclosure is at the Disclosing Party's cost.

findings.quote: within [[DEL: ten]] [[INS: fourteen]] Business Days of receipt of such request
findings.why: The return or destruction period moves from ten to fourteen Business Days, which is above the five Business Day minimum.
findings.fallback_cited: Any period of 5 Business Days or more.

findings.quote: copies of any Confidential Information that are securely stored in routine, automated electronic backup or archiving systems which are not readily accessible in the ordinary course of business
findings.why: The counterparty's margin comment asks whether automated 90-day cloud snapshots are covered; clause 6.2.1 already permits retention in automated backups, which stay confidential under 6.3.

findings.quote: All Confidential Information, and all intellectual property rights in or relating to it, shall remain the exclusive property of the Disclosing Party
findings.why: IP stays with the Disclosing Party and no licence is granted beyond use for the Purpose.

findings.quote: All Confidential Information is provided by the Disclosing Party on an "as is" basis.
findings.why: Information is provided as is with a mutual no-warranty statement, a reliance exclusion preserving fraud liability, and a no-obligation-to-proceed sentence.

findings.quote: Neither Party shall make, or permit any person to make, any public announcement, press release or other public disclosure
findings.why: Mutual publicity restriction requiring prior written consent, except as required by law.

findings.quote: that Party shall not disclose such personal data unless and until the Parties have agreed and entered into a separate written data processing agreement or data sharing agreement
findings.why: Personal data is limited to business contact details, with any further sharing only after a separate DPA or data sharing agreement.

findings.quote: for a period of two (2) years, unless terminated earlier by either Party giving not less than thirty (30) days' prior written notice
findings.why: Two-year term with 30 days' notice to terminate early matches the preferred position.

findings.quote: shall survive the expiry or termination of this Agreement for a period of three (3) years from the effective date of expiry or termination
findings.why: Three-year survival with Trade Secrets protected while they remain Trade Secrets is the preferred position; the counterparty's request to reduce to 2 years is within the accepted range and keeps Trade Secret protection.

findings.quote: a Party shall be entitled to seek the remedies of injunction, specific performance and other equitable relief
findings.why: Mutual right to seek injunctive and equitable relief, with cumulative remedies.

findings.quote: not reverse engineer, decompile, disassemble or otherwise attempt to derive the composition, source code or underlying structure of any software, prototypes or other tangible objects
findings.why: Reverse engineering of software and prototypes is prohibited.

findings.quote: Neither Party may assign, novate, transfer, mortgage, charge, subcontract, declare a trust over or deal in any other manner with any or all of its rights or obligations under this Agreement without the prior written consent of the other Party.
findings.why: No assignment by either Party without prior written consent.

findings.quote: governed by and construed in accordance with the law of England and Wales
findings.why: English law with exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of England and Wales.
